items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: You know after World War II there were the moldy figs, the ones that were interested in old records and King Oliver and Jelly Roll Morton and that kind of stuff

ctx.x: It was, yeah. I started a record company with him and then, well it’s too long a story. But I made a list of possible ideas for a small record company that the big ones aren’t doing so much, and that was one of them. I mean who would have known? I mean he actually followed it through, but it was something a small company could do that bigger ones don’t. So anyhow the music continues and you know I still consider myself a musician, I mean that’s what I’ve been doing for the sole of my existence for a long time…
